Package com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.infrastructure.tool

Class DelegateTool

java.lang.Object
com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.infrastructure.tool.DelegateTool
@Component public class DelegateTool extends Object
Spring AI bridge that exposes DelegationService.delegate(com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.application.chat.DelegationService.DelegationCommand) to the LLM as a tool-callable function (US-12-003, EPIC-12 TBD-3 resolution).

The @Tool-annotated method's name and description come from DelegationService.TOOL_NAME / DelegationService.TOOL_DESCRIPTION — both are compile-time String constants, so this annotation and DelegationService.DESCRIPTOR (used by ChatRequestBuilder to register the tool in the parent agent's ChatRequest.tools) cannot drift apart.

Deliberately NOT annotated with ToolGroup: the tool catalog (EPIC-07) does not list delegate. The descriptor is appended to ChatRequest.tools only when the parent agent's team is non-empty (the load-bearing runtime side of REQ-AGT-013 — a leaf agent simply never sees the descriptor and the LLM cannot call delegate(...) for it).

Context propagation: the parentAgentId and parentOwner inputs to DelegationService.DelegationCommand are NOT inputs from the LLM. They describe the current turn and are resolved through the request-scoped ChatTurnContext populated by SendMessageService. The LLM inputs are limited to targetMemberId (UUID string) and task (plain text) — both are validated and surfaced as a typed DelegationService.DelegationCommand.

Error mapping: malformed input from the LLM (non-UUID targetMemberId, blank/over-length task) raises a RuntimeException that propagates through Spring AI's tool dispatch into the parent's Reactor chain. The SSE error frame surfaces it as LLM_UNAVAILABLE 502 — "the model returned a malformed tool call" is an infrastructure failure of the model, not a user-input error. InvalidDelegationTargetException raised from DelegationService propagates the same way.
